I am trying to get some intuition in terms of prior for cholesky_factor_corr.

From the menu, i have seen cases where it has been given as lkj_corr_cholesky(4) and as lkj_corr_cholesky(2) (does it make a difference between the 2?)

Andy

On Tuesday, December 1, 2015 at 3:23:38 AM UTC-5, andy...@cubist-asia.com wrote:
I am trying to get some intuition in terms of prior for cholesky_factor_corr.

From the menu, i have seen cases where it has been given as lkj_corr_cholesky(4) and as lkj_corr_cholesky(2) (does it make a difference between the 2?)
Yes because it is an exponent. Usually it would be between 1 and 2.
When coding up multi-variate models, how should i around thinking about the eta parameter to the distribution?

See the discussion in the manual on interpreting the shape parameter in the LKJ distribution for a correlation matrix like the shape parameter of a univariate beta distribution. It is the same considerations for lkj_corr_cholesky().

Ben
